data.one_liner: A Flutter plugin for text-to-speech support across multiple platforms.
data.what_it_does: It allows your app to convert text into spoken audio, control speech rate, volume, and pitch, query available voices and languages, and synthesize text to a file across Android, iOS, Web, Windows, and macOS.
use_when: You need your Flutter app to read text out loud to users
You need to synthesize text into audio files on mobile platforms
avoid_when: You only need simple UI playback without text conversion features
You require complex server-side audio streaming pipelines
strengths: Supports a wide range of platforms including Android, iOS, Web, Windows, and macOS
Provides fine-grained control over speech properties like pitch, rate, volume, and specific voices
weaknesses: Requires platform-specific configuration such as updating the minimum Android SDK or Kotlin versions
Some advanced features like pause/resume or speech marks have platform-specific restrictions or workarounds
data.setup_notes: Requires Android minimum SDK 21 and Kotlin version 1.9.10 updates. Android 11+ target apps need an intent action declaration in the manifest for TTS service queries.
